md_description: This workflow follows agricultural soil samples from plots managed under conventional tillage, no-till, and organic farming through homogenization, DNA extraction, ITS amplicon sequencing, and soil physicochemical assays. It produces raw sequencing reads, fungal community derivatives, and soil chemistry derivatives that are integrated to assess how farming practices influence fungal diversity, soil health, and productivity.

agricultural_plot_soil_samples.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic sample identity/origin fields that describe what the composite soil samples are and where they came from. I excluded any homogenization, extraction, assay, sequencing, or downstream analysis details because those belong to Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. Since this is the root sample node and no overlapping fields were indicated in already_generated, I used core provenance fields needed to distinguish plots and farming practices without repeating downstream measurements.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for each composite agricultural soil sample; use a stable string such as 'AS-001'. Assigned at collection and used to link the sample through downstream homogenization, DNA extraction, sequencing, and chemistry workflows.
Identifier of the agricultural field plot from which the composite soil sample was collected; use a stable string such as 'PLOT-12'. Recorded at sampling to preserve plot-level provenance.

Agricultural management practice applied to the source plot at the time of sampling. Recorded for the originating plot, not as an assay result. Allowed values: conventional_tillage, no_till, organic_farming.
Date the composite soil sample was collected from the plot, recorded at field sampling. Use ISO 8601 date format, for example 2026-08-18.

Soil depth interval represented by the composite sample at collection, in centimeters. Report as a depth range or target depth in the collection record, for example 0-15 cm if the field protocol uses a shallow topsoil composite.

General soil classification or field soil description for the sampled plot, recorded at collection as an intrinsic site/sample property. Use a controlled term where possible, for example 'loam' or 'sandy_loam'.

Physical condition of the composite soil sample at receipt or collection, describing the material state relevant to handling before homogenization. Allowed values: fresh, field_frozen, air_dried, refrigerated.

soil_homogenization_and_subsampling.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only fields describing how the soil homogenization and subsampling operation was performed and the operating conditions that affect the prepared aliquots. I excluded sample identity, plot provenance, and soil chemistry outputs because those belong to the upstream Entity and downstream Derivative nodes. I also avoided DNA extraction and assay details because those are separate downstream processes. No already_generated overlap was provided for this step, so I focused on protocol parameters and a process quality indicator needed for reproducibility.

md_schema.descr: Method used to homogenize the composite soil sample before aliquoting, recorded during the processing step. Allowed values: manual_mixing, mechanical_mixing, sieving_and_mixing, bead_assisted_mixing.

Target mass of each soil aliquot prepared from the homogenized sample for downstream DNA extraction and physicochemical assays, measured during subsampling. Typical range in this workflow is 0.1-10 g depending on downstream input needs.
Total time spent homogenizing the soil before subsampling, recorded during the processing step. Typical range is 1-60 minutes depending on sample volume and method.

Temperature of the sample during homogenization and subsampling, measured or maintained during processing. Typical range is 4-25 C, depending on whether processing is done chilled or at room temperature.

Number of aliquots generated from each homogenized soil sample for downstream workflows, recorded at the end of the processing step. Typical values are 1 or greater, depending on how many downstream analyses are planned.
Operational assessment of whether the homogenized soil appeared uniform enough for downstream aliquoting, recorded after processing. Allowed values: pass, warning, fail.

homogenized_soil_aliquot.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared soil aliquot itself: its identity, physical amount, storage state, and handling provenance after subsampling. I excluded homogenization protocol details because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded DNA extraction and physicochemical assay parameters because those belong downstream. No already_generated fields were provided for this node, so I focused on the minimum aliquot descriptors needed to connect downstream extraction and soil assays reproducibly.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared homogenized soil aliquot; use a stable string such as 'ALIQUOT-001'. Assigned immediately after subsampling and used to link the aliquot to downstream DNA extraction and soil parameter assays.

Mass of the prepared soil aliquot in grams, measured after subsampling and before downstream processing. Typical range is 0.1-10 g depending on whether the aliquot is used for extraction or chemistry assays.
Storage condition of the prepared aliquot between subsampling and downstream use. Allowed values: immediate_use, refrigerated, frozen, room_temperature.

Storage temperature of the prepared soil aliquot during short-term holding before downstream processing, measured at storage. Typical range is -80 to 25 C depending on whether the aliquot is frozen, refrigerated, or held briefly at room temperature.

Container type used to hold the homogenized soil aliquot before downstream processing, recorded at preparation. Use a controlled term or descriptive string such as '2 ml microcentrifuge tube' or 'sterile_whirl_pak_bag'.
Date the homogenized soil aliquot was prepared from the composite sample. Use ISO 8601 date format, for example 2026-08-18.

dna_extraction_from_soil.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only extraction protocol parameters, reagent/kit details, and a process-level yield/quality indicator that describe how microbial DNA was obtained from the soil aliquot. I excluded aliquot identity and storage because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded DNA extract properties such as concentration or purity because those belong to the downstream Entity node. No already_generated fields were provided here, so I focused on the minimum reproducible extraction metadata needed before ITS library preparation.

md_schema.descr: Name of the DNA extraction kit or protocol used to isolate microbial DNA from the soil aliquot, recorded during the extraction process. Use a specific product or protocol name such as 'DNeasy PowerSoil Pro Kit'.
Manufacturer of the DNA extraction kit or consumables used in the extraction step, recorded during processing. Use the vendor name, for example 'Qiagen' or 'MO BIO'.
Mass of homogenized soil aliquot loaded into the extraction workflow, measured at the start of DNA extraction. Typical range is 0.1-5 g depending on kit and protocol.
Primary lysis approach used to break cells and release DNA during extraction. Allowed values: bead_beating, chemical_lysis, enzymatic_lysis, combined_lysis.
Final elution volume used to recover DNA from the extraction column or matrix, measured at the end of extraction. Typical range is 20-200 uL.
Total amount of recovered DNA measured after extraction and before library preparation, typically determined by fluorometric or spectrophotometric quantification. Typical range is 0-1000 ng.
Assessment of whether the extracted DNA was suitable for downstream ITS library preparation, recorded after extraction. Allowed values: pass, warning, fail.

soil_dna_extract.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the recovered soil DNA extract: its identity, concentration, purity, fragment integrity, and storage/handling status before library preparation. I excluded the extraction kit, lysis method, and yield because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded library construction details because those belong downstream. No already_generated fields were provided for this node, so I selected the minimum extract descriptors needed for assessing suitability for ITS amplicon library preparation.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the recovered soil DNA extract; use a stable string such as 'DNA-001'. Assigned after extraction and used to link the extract to ITS library preparation.
Measured DNA concentration of the extract in ng per uL, determined after extraction and before library preparation. Typical range for soil extracts is 0-500 ng per uL.
Total mass of DNA recovered in the extract, calculated from concentration and elution volume or measured directly after extraction. Typical range for soil extracts is 0-1000 ng.
Spectrophotometric purity ratio of the DNA extract measured after extraction and before library preparation. Typical range is 1.6-2.1 for relatively clean DNA extracts.
Qualitative assessment of extract fragment integrity or shearing state made before library preparation. Allowed values: intact, moderately_sheared, heavily_sheared, not_assessed.
Storage condition of the DNA extract before library preparation. Allowed values: immediate_use, refrigerated, frozen.
Storage temperature of the DNA extract during holding before ITS library preparation, measured at storage. Typical range is -80 to 8 C depending on frozen or refrigerated storage.

its_amplicon_library_prep.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only library preparation parameters describing how the ITS amplicon library was generated from the soil DNA extract: primer choice, PCR/indexing setup, cycle conditions, cleanup, and a process-level quality indicator. I excluded DNA extract intrinsic properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded library product properties such as concentration, fragment size, or pooling status because those belong to the downstream ITS amplicon library Entity. No already_generated overlap was provided for this node, so I focused on reproducible PCR and indexing details.

md_schema.descr: Fungal ITS subregion amplified during library preparation, recorded at the amplification step. Allowed values: ITS1, ITS2, full_its, other.
Forward primer sequence used to amplify the fungal ITS region, recorded during library preparation. Provide the nucleotide sequence string, for example 'CTTGGTCATTTAGAGGAAGTAA'.
Reverse primer sequence used to amplify the fungal ITS region, recorded during library preparation. Provide the nucleotide sequence string, for example 'GCTGCGTTCTTCATCGATGC'.
Number of PCR cycles used to amplify and index the ITS library, recorded during library preparation. Typical range is 15-40 cycles.
Annealing temperature used during ITS amplification PCR, recorded during the amplification step. Typical range is 45-72 C.
Indexing approach used to multiplex libraries for sequencing. Allowed values: single_index, dual_index, inline_barcode, no_index.
Cleanup method used after ITS amplification and indexing, recorded before the library is passed downstream. Allowed values: magnetic_bead_cleanup, gel_extraction, enzymatic_cleanup, none.
Post-preparation assessment of whether the indexed ITS amplicon library was suitable for sequencing, recorded at the end of library preparation. Allowed values: pass, warning, fail.

its_amplicon_library.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared ITS amplicon library itself: library identity, concentration, fragment-size characteristics, indexing identity, and storage status before sequencing. I excluded PCR primers, cycle counts, and cleanup method because those belong to the upstream library-preparation Process node, and I excluded sequencing run settings because those belong to the downstream Capture node. No already_generated fields were provided for this node, so I selected the minimum library descriptors needed for loading the sequencer reproducibly.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared ITS amplicon library; use a stable string such as 'ITS-LIB-001'. Assigned after library preparation and used to connect the library to the sequencing run.
Measured concentration of the prepared ITS amplicon library in ng per uL, determined after cleanup and before sequencing. Typical range is 0-100 ng per uL.

Representative amplicon fragment size in base pairs for the prepared ITS library, measured after library preparation and before sequencing. Typical fungal ITS libraries range from about 150 to 800 bp depending on targeted subregion and primers.

Spectrophotometric or fluorometric purity indicator for the prepared library measured before sequencing, typically reported as an A260/A280-like ratio or equivalent cleanup quality metric. Typical range is 1.6-2.2.

Identifier for the barcode or index sequence set incorporated into the prepared library, recorded after indexing and before sequencing. Use a string such as 'N701/S501' or a vendor-specific index set name.
Storage condition of the prepared ITS amplicon library prior to sequencing. Allowed values: immediate_use, refrigerated, frozen.
Storage temperature of the prepared ITS amplicon library while awaiting sequencing, measured at storage. Typical range is -80 to 8 C depending on frozen or refrigerated holding.

illuminasequencer_its_run.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration fields for the Illumina sequencing run: instrument identity, model/serial/manufacturer, run chemistry, read structure, lane/loading settings, and run-level quality indicators. I excluded sample/library intrinsic properties because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded file-specific properties such as FASTQ size or path because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided software details here because the capture node should describe the hardware and configured run, not downstream processing software. No already_generated overlap was provided for this node.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the ITS run, recorded as part of the capture setup. For this workflow it is typically 'Illumina'.
Instrument model used to read the ITS amplicon library, recorded at the start of the sequencing session. Use a specific model name such as 'MiSeq' or 'NextSeq 550'.
Serial number of the sequencing instrument used for the run, recorded for instrument traceability at capture. Use the manufacturer-assigned serial string, for example 'M01234'.
Flow cell or cartridge type installed for the ITS sequencing run, recorded during instrument setup. Use a vendor-specific term such as 'MiSeq Reagent Kit v3'.
Sequencing chemistry selected for the capture session, recorded during run setup. Allowed values: single_end, paired_end, mate_pair.
Configured read length in base pairs for each sequencing read, measured as part of the run setup. Typical values for ITS amplicons are 150-300 bp per read.
Final loading concentration of the ITS amplicon library applied to the sequencer, recorded during instrument configuration. Typical range is 1-20 pM depending on platform and library complexity.
Lane or run partition used for the ITS library on the instrument, recorded during the capture session. Use an integer lane number if applicable; for single-lane instruments record 1.

Operational assessment of the sequencing run quality at completion, based on instrument-level metrics such as cluster density, percent bases Q30, or run completion status. Allowed values: pass, warning, fail.

raw_its_fastq.reasoning: I corrected the Signal-node schema by removing the colliding field read_length_bp, which had already been generated elsewhere in the DAG. I kept only raw-read artefact properties that remain within the Signal node territory: file identity, format, size, read structure, read count, quality, checksum, and storage location. I did not add capture settings or downstream processed-output properties.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw FASTQ read file or file pair; use a stable string such as 'FASTQ-001'. Assigned when raw sequencing data are generated and stored.
File format of the raw reads produced by the sequencing run. Allowed values: fastq, gzipped_fastq, bcl_converted_fastq.
Total size of the raw FASTQ file or file set in bytes, recorded from the stored artefact. Typical range is 0-100000000000 depending on run scale.
Read structure present in the raw sequence artefact. Allowed values: paired_end, single_end.
Total number of reads contained in the raw FASTQ artefact, counted from the file after sequencing. Typical range is 0-100000000.
Average base-level Phred quality score across the raw FASTQ reads, calculated from the file as a technical quality metric. Typical range is 0-40.
MD5 checksum of the FASTQ artefact used to verify file integrity after transfer or storage. Use a 32-character hexadecimal string, for example 'd41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e'.
Storage location of the raw FASTQ artefact in a local or remote repository, recorded as a URI or path string such as 's3://bucket/run1/reads.fastq.gz' or '/data/reads.fastq.gz'.

soil_parameter_assays.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the assay session and instrument-configuration fields for the physicochemical measurements performed on the homogenized soil aliquot. I focused on the configured instruments, assay methods, calibration/QA status, and measured settings that define how moisture, organic matter, and nutrient values were obtained. I excluded the actual assay outputs such as moisture percentage or nutrient concentrations because those belong to the downstream Derivative node, and I excluded sample identity and aliquot properties because those belong upstream. I also avoided field names that could collide with previously generated DAG fields, including read_length_bp, and did not reuse any sequence-capture terms.

md_schema.descr: Name of the analytical instrument used for the soil physicochemical assay session, recorded as part of the capture configuration. Use a specific instrument name such as 'Karl Fischer titrator', 'CHN analyzer', or 'ICP-MS'.
Manufacturer of the laboratory instrument used for soil parameter measurements, recorded during assay setup. Use the vendor name, for example 'Thermo Fisher', 'Agilent', or 'Mettler Toledo'.
Model of the analytical instrument used for the soil assay session, recorded at measurement time. Use a specific model name such as 'iCAP Q', '8400S', or an equivalent vendor model.
Serial number of the analytical instrument used for the soil parameter assays, recorded for traceability at capture. Use the manufacturer-assigned serial string.

Primary assay method used to quantify soil moisture, organic matter, or nutrient levels from the homogenized soil aliquot, recorded during the capture session. Use a controlled method name such as 'gravimetric moisture', 'loss_on_ignition', 'colorimetric_nutrient_assay', or 'icp_elemental_analysis'.
Whether the analytical instrument and assay were calibrated/verified immediately before the measurement session. Allowed values: calibrated, verification_passed, verification_failed, not_recorded.
Operational quality-control outcome for the soil assay session, based on blanks, standards, or replicate checks performed at measurement time. Allowed values: pass, warning, fail.

Ambient or controlled temperature during the soil physicochemical measurement session, recorded at the time of assay. Typical range is 15-30 C depending on laboratory conditions and method requirements.
Identifier of the analytical batch or plate/run used to process the soil measurements, recorded during capture for traceability. Use a stable string such as 'SOIL-BATCH-01'.

soil_physical_chemistry_table.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed result fields describing the soil chemistry table itself: table identity, row/column dimensions, which variables are present, units/completeness, and table-level quality indicators. I excluded assay instrument settings because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded the underlying measured concentrations or moisture values because those are the contents of the table rather than metadata about the table. I also avoided reusing any previously generated field names from other steps.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived soil chemistry table; use a stable string such as 'SOIL-CHEM-001'. Assigned when the quantitative table is assembled from assay outputs.
Number of sample records contained in the soil chemistry table, counted after derivation. Typical range is 1 to the total number of sampled plots or aliquots in the dataset.
Number of data columns in the derived soil chemistry table, counted after derivation. Typical range is 1-100 depending on the number of soil variables and identifiers included.

List of soil property variables represented in the derived table, recorded at the time of table creation. Typical entries include moisture_content, organic_matter, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and other nutrient metrics.
Unit system used for quantitative values in the soil chemistry table, recorded when the derivative is created. Use a concise descriptor such as 'percent_and_mg_per_kg' or 'SI'.
Fraction of table cells with missing or unreported values, calculated after assembly of the derivative table. Typical range is 0.0-1.0.
Overall assessment of the derived soil chemistry table quality after assembly and basic validation. Allowed values: pass, warning, fail.

Storage location of the derived soil chemistry table in a local or remote repository, recorded as a URI or path string such as 's3://bucket/soil/soil_chemistry_table.csv' or '/data/soil_chemistry_table.tsv'.

its_read_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only read-processing workflow parameters and a process-level quality indicator: software/pipeline identity, version, filtering and denoising settings, merge and chimera options, and the processing output criteria used to generate high-quality ITS features. I excluded raw FASTQ properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded feature table properties such as row counts or taxonomy because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. No already_generated overlaps were provided for this node, so I focused on reproducible processing parameters while avoiding sequence-capture terms already used elsewhere.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to process ITS reads, recorded for the read-processing step. Examples include 'QIIME 2', 'DADA2', or 'USEARCH'.
Version of the read-processing software or pipeline, recorded during processing for reproducibility. Use a version string such as '2024.2' or '1.30.0'.
Read structure expected by the processing workflow at the start of filtering and denoising. Allowed values: paired_end, single_end.
Minimum base-quality threshold used to filter ITS reads before denoising, recorded as part of the processing parameters. Typical range is 10-40 Phred.
Read truncation length applied during quality filtering or denoising, measured in base pairs and recorded at processing time. Typical range is 0-300 bp depending on read quality.
Method used to identify and remove chimeric reads during ITS processing. Allowed values: consensus, de_novo, reference_based, hybrid.
Algorithm used to infer high-quality ITS features from filtered reads. Allowed values: dada2, deblur, swarm, otu_clustering, other.
Overall assessment of whether the processed reads were suitable for downstream feature table construction, recorded at the end of processing. Allowed values: pass, warning, fail.

fungal_feature_table.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only properties of the computed fungal feature table itself: table identity, feature definition, dimensions, sparsity, normalization state, taxonomy linkage status, and table-level quality/relational metadata. I excluded read-processing parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded diversity statistics because those belong to the downstream derivative analysis node. No already_generated fields were provided for this node, so I selected the minimum table descriptors needed to reuse the abundance matrix for downstream ecological analysis.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed fungal feature table; use a stable string such as 'FT-001'. Assigned when the abundance matrix is created from processed ITS reads.
Definition of the units represented in the feature table, recorded at derivation time. Allowed values: asv, otu, exact_sequence_variant, other.
Number of soil samples represented as rows or columns in the feature table, counted after table construction. Typical range is 1 to the total number of samples in the study.
Number of ITS features represented in the table, counted after processing and feature inference. Typical range is 1-100000 depending on clustering or denoising strategy.
Fraction of matrix cells with nonzero abundance values, calculated after table construction as a sparsity measure. Typical range is 0.0-1.0.
Whether the abundance values are raw counts or transformed values in the derived table. Allowed values: raw_counts, rarefied_counts, relative_abundance, compositional_transformed, other.
Status of downstream taxonomy assignment for the feature table at the time this derivative is stored. Allowed values: not_assigned, partially_assigned, fully_assigned.
Overall assessment of the computed feature table quality after construction, including whether it is complete and usable for downstream diversity analysis. Allowed values: pass, warning, fail.
Storage location of the derived fungal feature table in a local or remote repository, recorded as a URI or path string such as 's3://bucket/its/feature_table.tsv' or '/data/feature_table.qza'.

community_diversity_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only diversity-analysis workflow parameters and software configuration: the analysis package, version, normalization approach inherited by the workflow configuration, and the specific alpha/beta metric choices used to compute diversity summaries from the fungal feature table. I excluded the feature table's intrinsic properties because those belong to the upstream Derivative node, and I excluded the resulting diversity values because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. No already_generated overlaps were provided for this node, so I focused on reproducible analysis settings and a process-level quality check.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to calculate community diversity metrics from the fungal feature table, recorded at the start of the analysis step. Examples include 'QIIME 2', 'phyloseq', or 'vegan'.
Version of the diversity analysis software or pipeline, recorded for reproducibility. Use a version string such as '2024.2' or '2.6-6'.
Type of abundance table used as input for the diversity calculations, recorded at analysis time. Allowed values: raw_counts, rarefied_counts, relative_abundance, compositional_transformed, other.
Primary alpha diversity metric calculated from the fungal feature table, recorded during analysis. Allowed values: observed_features, shannon, simpson, faith_pd, chao1, evenness, other.

Primary beta diversity distance or dissimilarity metric calculated from the fungal feature table, recorded during analysis. Allowed values: bray_curtis, jaccard, unweighted_unifrac, weighted_unifrac, euclidean, other.
Rarefaction depth used, if applicable, before diversity calculations, recorded at analysis time. Typical range is 0-100000 reads per sample depending on dataset depth and retention goals.
Ordination method used for beta diversity visualization or summarization, if performed during the analysis step. Allowed values: pcoa, nmds, permenova_only, other.
Overall assessment of whether the diversity analysis completed successfully and produced interpretable metrics, recorded at the end of the process. Allowed values: pass, warning, fail.

fungal_diversity_metrics.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only properties of the computed diversity result object: metric identity, which alpha/beta summaries are included, result grouping basis, and result-level quality/storage metadata. I excluded the analysis pipeline settings because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded the numerical diversity values themselves because those are the contents of the derivative, not metadata describing the derivative. I also removed sample_count to avoid collision with a previously generated field in this DAG, and kept the remaining field names distinct from prior steps.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived fungal diversity metrics object; use a stable string such as 'DIV-001'. Assigned when diversity summaries are computed from the fungal feature table.

List of alpha diversity metrics included in the derived result set, recorded when the derivative is created. Typical entries include observed_features, shannon, simpson, chao1, faith_pd, and evenness.
List of beta diversity metrics included in the derived result set, recorded when the derivative is created. Typical entries include bray_curtis, jaccard, unweighted_unifrac, and weighted_unifrac.
Experimental grouping variable used to summarize or compare diversity results, recorded at derivation time. For this workflow it is typically the farming practice classification of the source plot.
Number of distinct groups represented in the diversity summary, counted from the grouping variable. Typical value range is 2-10 depending on experimental design.
Method used to assemble the reported diversity summaries from the metric outputs, recorded when the derivative is created. Allowed values: per_sample, grouped_summary, model_based_summary, other.
Overall assessment of the derived fungal diversity metrics quality after computation and validation. Allowed values: pass, warning, fail.

Storage location of the derived fungal diversity metrics object in a local or remote repository, recorded as a URI or path string such as 's3://bucket/its/diversity_metrics.tsv' or '/data/diversity_metrics.rds'.

soil_fungal_association_modeling.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only modeling workflow parameters and software configuration used to integrate the soil chemistry derivatives with fungal diversity metrics. I focused on the statistical framework, covariates, response and predictor specification, transformation choices, and a process-level model fit/diagnostic indicator. I excluded the input table properties because those belong to upstream Derivative nodes, and I excluded the computed association results because those belong downstream. I also avoided reusing collision-prone generic names already generated elsewhere in the DAG, including sample_count, and selected fields that are specific to the modeling step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or statistical environment used to run the soil-fungal association model, recorded during the modeling process. Examples include 'R', 'RStudio', 'lme4', or 'vegan'.
Version of the software or environment used for association modeling, recorded for reproducibility. Use a version string such as '4.4.0'.

Set of fungal diversity outcomes used as responses in the association model, recorded at model specification time. Typical values include alpha diversity metrics, beta diversity axes, or grouped diversity summaries; provide a concise descriptive string.

Set of soil chemistry variables used as predictors in the association model, recorded at model specification time. Typical values include moisture content, organic matter, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and other nutrient measurements; provide a concise descriptive string.

Primary statistical model used to test associations between soil properties and fungal community change. Allowed values: linear_model, mixed_effects_model, correlation_analysis, redundancy_analysis, permutation_test, other.
Transformation applied to one or more variables before modeling, recorded at analysis time. Allowed values: none, log_transform, z_score, centered, clr_transform, other.
Correction method used for multiple hypothesis testing in the association modeling workflow, recorded if significance testing was performed. Allowed values: none, fdr_bh, bonferroni, holm, other.
Overall assessment of whether the association model converged and passed basic diagnostic checks at the end of the process. Allowed values: pass, warning, fail.

soil_fungal_correlation_results.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only properties of the computed statistical results object: result identity, model type, relationship family, effect-size and significance descriptors, and result-level quality/storage metadata. I excluded upstream modeling configuration and raw inputs because those belong to the Process node and upstream Derivative nodes. I also removed the colliding field grouping_variable, since it was already generated earlier in the DAG, and replaced it with a more specific result-level descriptor to keep the metadata flat and non-duplicative.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the derived soil-fungal correlation results object; use a stable string such as 'CORR-001'. Assigned when statistical association outputs are generated.
Type of statistical association analysis represented by the result object. Allowed values: correlation, linear_model, mixed_effects_model, redundancy_analysis, permutation_test, other.

Textual summary of the main effect size or association direction reported by the result object, recorded after computation. Provide a concise string such as 'positive association with soil moisture' or 'small negative correlation with nitrogen'.
Textual summary of statistical significance for the reported associations, recorded after computation. Provide a concise string such as 'p < 0.05 after FDR correction' or 'not significant'.

Concise description of the fungal diversity responses and soil property predictors linked in the derived result object, recorded at result creation. Use a short string such as 'fungal alpha diversity vs moisture and organic matter'.
Description of the farming-practice comparison basis represented in the result object, recorded at result creation. Use a concise string such as 'conventional_tillage vs no_till vs organic_farming'.
Overall assessment of whether the derived association results are coherent and suitable for interpretation, recorded after validation of the statistical output. Allowed values: pass, warning, fail.

Storage location of the derived statistical results in a local or remote repository, recorded as a URI or path string such as 's3://bucket/its/correlation_results.rds' or '/data/correlation_results.csv'.
